findings: Both captures describe a customer authorizing an e-mandate during initial setup in the UPI app with PIN additional factor authentication. An existing mandate allows future automated charges within its terms. Stripe handles the initial charge window of up to five minutes and, with SetupIntent, debits and instantly refunds to avoid requiring AFA for the intended later charge. This does not remove PIN authorization during mandate setup.

Merchant confirms a PaymentIntent for a subsequent recurring payment, which triggers Stripe to send the customer an SMS/app notification with exact debit amount and mandate cancellation option, wait at least 24 hours and then charge. No additional merchant actions are documented after confirmation. Notification and waiting are separate from a successful charge outcome.

Both list the same `payment_method_options[upi][mandate_options]` defaults: customer-visible description Subscription, `amount=1500000` in minor units (15,000 INR maximum for automatic AutoPay charges), amount_type maximum or merchant-selected fixed, and 10-year expiry with a 40-year from-now scheme maximum.

With a customer-initiated Adaptive Pricing subscription, automatic e-mandate creation in the selected currency is conditional on mandate support for it. If explicit Checkout Session mandate parameters are provided, they override automatically determined values. The guide tells users seeking the local-currency and exchange-rate handling to omit such parameters.

The rebased capture metadata, numbered list serialization and table padding are presentation. The linked Adaptive Pricing and supported mandate currency authorities remain the same links and supply no independently verified currency list here.
